prompts: Shot 1 opens with establishing space, wide shot, eye-level with slight downward angle, slowly pushing in from the edge of a high-rise rooftop. Foreground shows rain-soaked railing and scattered droplets; background features layered neon buildings and hazy light spots. Composition places a young woman slightly off-center, standing still in starting position, single sword hanging at her side before slowly lifting it. Neon side-lighting outlines her silhouette and sword spine with cold highlights. Puddles reflect fragmented ad colors. Camera push-in synchronizes with her inhalation during the start-up motion.

Shot 2 hard-cut from previous shot, close-up, eye-level. Camera continues forward push and slight right pan from chest level, focusing on the sword hand, wrist, and side profile of the face. Shallow depth of field blurs background neon into flowing color patches. Still on the rooftop, but distance shortened sharply to emphasize detail. She completes cloud-hand wrist turn, elbow and shoulder coordination creating sword path, then executes a straight thrust. Blade slices through rain mist, forming a brief sharp bright trail. Wrist movement is precise, forearm muscles tighten, sleeve edges generate micro-air waves. Lighting continues with neon side-lighting; sword surface occasionally reflects flashing white from ad lights.

Shot 3 hard-cut from previous shot, close-up, overhead view. Camera follows her into a wet narrow alley from above, first short overhead tracking, then slight orbiting. Uses wall and ground reflections to create strong leading lines. Foreground shows dangling wires and dripping water; She continuously spins and draws flower patterns along the alley, steps compact yet stable, weight shifts clearly visible. Shoes glide over puddles, creating arcing water trails that ripple outward. Sword movements align coaxially with body rotation. Hair tips and sleeves show natural lag at end of spin. Overall lighting remains within neutral night tone and neon reflection balance. Wet walls reflect intermittent color blocks.

Shot 4 hard-cut from previous shot, medium shot, low-angle. Scene progresses logically to an elevated walkway. Camera tracks upward from low angle with brief zoom-in. Background includes upper traffic light strips and large ad screens. Walkway railings create depth perspective. Character reaches action climax: first holds lunge downward slash, sword creates clear descending trajectory, then uses waist and hips to turn and block. Motion is crisp and decisive. Front foot lands, shaking residual water. Ad screen reflection flashes across blade surface, creating a brief sharp highlight.

Shot 5 fade in/out transition from previous shot, extreme close-up to pull-out, eye-level. Small plaza scene connects to walkway exit. Camera initially focuses on her hand, guard, and slightly rising chest, then slowly pulls back to medium-close. Foreground shows shallow puddle and scattered light spots at plaza edge; background features open urban interface and blurred silhouettes of distant pedestrians. Sleeves stop large swings, only slight flutter from post-rain breeze remains. Water surface ripples slowly outward after final step. Lighting maintains consistent neon and reflection base, brightness slightly softened for calm ending. Image and

prompts: Shot 1 fades in from black, a wide eye-level composition includes the subway station exterior entrance, railings, and descending steps. Railing lines form leading lines directing attention to the young female dancer on the right. Foreground shows slightly blurred handrails, background reveals gray-blue urban morning air. Side lighting glides over her calves and jacket edges. She stretches, taps toes, shoulders and back subtly rise and fall, jacket flutters with motion. The camera slowly pushes in as the Spanish female

Shot 2 connects to the previous shot via a hard cut, switching to a medium tracking eye-level shot, moving diagonally through the turnstile. Metal frames of the turnstile create foreground-background layering. Focus locks onto the young female dancer’s face and upper body just after passing through. Cold white light highlights her tense and focused expression. As she looks up, she briefly makes eye contact with another female dancer across the passage. The other dancer stops for half a second, chin slightly raised, clearly establishing competitive tension. The camera moves sideways with their crossing paths.

Shot 3 enters the open transfer hall via a hard cut, medium eye-level shot shifting to a slight low angle. Floor tile patterns serve as vanishing lines pointing directly to the protagonist. Background columns and signage provide stable spatial reference. Cold white ceiling lights cast soft reflections on the floor. She quickly lowers her center of gravity, starting with a six-step floor move, hands pressing the ground, legs crossing in circles, toes scraping the floor forming continuous arcs. The Spanish female

Shot 4 cuts sharply via action match to an overhead close-up. The frame retains only hands, wrists, shoulders, and partial ground. Tile seam lines form a cross-shaped compositional center. Focus sharply presses on the supporting hand and forearm muscles. Sweat begins to appear under cold light. Her palm suddenly presses firmly into the ground, shoulders engage, smoothly transitioning into a coffee grinder. During single-leg spinning, pants hem and shoelaces are lifted by centrifugal force. The camera remains fixed overhead with minimal follow.

Shot 5 cuts sharply to the other female dancer’s medium-close low-angle shot. Foreground blurs the protagonist’s leg withdrawal. Focus lands on the opponent’s torso and rotating legs. Environment remains the same transfer hall. Fluorescent lights create brief highlights during rotation. She almost without pause drops into the ground, countering with a windmill, shoulders and back rolling along the ground, legs fully extended forming a windmill-like loop. Jacket hem swings out clearly, leaving a distinct trail. The camera performs a brief lateral pan following her rotation direction, enhancing the impact of the counterattack.

Shot 6 connects to the previous shot via a quick whip pan transition, returning to the protagonist. Close eye-level slightly low-angle shot. Composition places protagonist in the left foreground, opponent’s half-body retained in the right background for relational context. Cold environment unchanged but floor reflection more prominent. She uses the momentum of the opponent’s move to slide in, body leaning sideways, quickly entering a swipe. The camera first pans to follow, then slightly pushes in.

Shot 7 cuts sharply from the previous shot to a low-angle close-up. Camera nearly touches the ground looking upward. Protagonist occupies the center of the frame. Top fluorescent lights and high signage form upward-extending background, leading lines focusing on her grounded pose. After a series of flips, she abruptly freezes into a baby freeze, elbow pivot stable, neck, shoulders, and core muscles visibly tensed. Face bears sharp, determined smile after effort, sweat droplet sliding down temple. Spanish female The camera performs a slight push-in, intensifying the frozen action’s pressure and suspense of outcome.

Shot 8 transitions via a brief fade-in/fade-out to a distant overhead view at the stairwell entrance. The space reopens, handrails and floor warning lines forming a circular visual guide. Protagonist and opponent are centered, surrounding pedestrians drawn in instinctively step back, gradually forming a loose circle. Partially blurred suitcase edge in foreground, flickering train information screen in background. Cold white ceiling lights and distant side fill maintain uniform gray-blue ambiance. The camera slowly pulls out.

Shot 9 cuts sharply to a medium eye-level low-angle shot in the platform waiting area. Train tracks and platform columns create strong perspective. Focus tightly locks on protagonist’s full-body motion. Background features opponent and onlookers in clear but unobtrusive layers. Under the same cold white fluorescent light, she unleashes consecutive flares, legs widely spread and spinning rapidly, body weight fluidly shifting between arms. After several spins, she directly transitions into a one-arm support, wrist pressing firmly, core tightened, shoes leaving brief motion trails. The camera initially follows sideways, then quickly pushes in at the final support point. Female Deep wind

Background platform light strips blur into soft bokeh. Focus first lands on protagonist’s sweat droplet sliding down temple and smiling lips, then gently shifts to the other dancer’s similarly relieved expression. Both synchronize their finishing poses, stepping forward to lightly bump fists, shoulders finally relaxing. Fabric and hair slowly settle. The camera gently pulls back half a step to conclude. Spanish

prompts: Shot 1 opens with a fade-in, wide overhead view of the dawn courtyard. Foreground shows gently swaying pixel flags; background includes stone towers and arches lightly veiled in morning mist. Composition uses flagpole and brick ground vanishing lines to guide focus toward the runners. Warm dawn light illuminates character edges from behind and side, while flickering torch embers add highlights in shadows. Bread swings short arms, cheese crouches into starting position. The camera slightly tilts down then slowly pushes in, building anticipation for the race start.

Shot 2 connects to previous shot via a hard cut triggered by the starting motion, medium eye-level tracking shot moving into the torch-lit corridor. Foreground occasionally sweeps past flickering flames and stone pillars; midground locks onto the bread runner sprinting ahead; background stone walls display magical runes flashing sequentially along the running path, creating strong depth. Strong leading lines from floor tiles and walls enhance perspective. Medium depth of field keeps both runner and wall runes sharp. Lighting remains warm torchlight mixed with soft dawn glow. Apple and cheese briefly appear behind, forming chase layers. Small accessories like cloth flaps and crumbs vibrate with speed. Camera tracks along the path with slight forward follow, enhancing speed sensation.

Shot 3 transitions from previous shot via a momentum-driven hard cut to a higher vantage point, overhead wide shot covering the complex route of suspension bridge connecting to spiral staircase. Foreground shows wooden planks and iron chains; midground features the cheese runner climbing strenuously; background reveals castle outer walls and lower courtyard bathed in golden dawn light. Lighting continues warm tone, with deeper contrast only in bridge shadows. Body shifts slightly forward, wooden planks tremble beneath feet, chains sway. Apple and bread flash past frame edges, creating pursuit pressure. Lute inserts denser, shorter plucks here; bellows hiss and bridge groans align precisely with climbing motions. Camera slowly descends from above the bridge and gently rotates along the stair arc, emphasizing vertical drop and physical exertion.

Shot 4 enters via a hard cut after corner obstruction, close-up eye-level shot transitioning to push-in at the armory’s exterior corner. Foreground shows hanging weapons and partially focused chains; midground features the apple runner suddenly cutting inside the corner and accelerating to overtake; background shows standing armor units trembling from airflow and vibration. Composition uses wall-floor intersection to direct focus toward the turn apex. Shallow depth of field emphasizes apple’s expression and motion. Warm torchlight creates dancing reflections on metal armor. Apple’s eyes are focused, leg stride increases, body leans sharply through the turn. Camera first moves short distance laterally, then abruptly pushes in on apple’s face, creating explosive overtaking impact.

Foreground shows wind-fluttering colored flags and finish banner; background features fully illuminated tower peak and distant city walls in dawn light. Flagpoles and eaves create upward leading lines, emphasizing victory. Deep depth of field ensures full visibility of finish environment. Lighting remains consistent warm gold; backlight outlines the runners’ edges. Brief suspension before landing causes flags, knots, and small debris to tremble in air. Cheers synchronize with characters’ open-mouthed shouting expressions. Camera quickly pushes in from low angle, then slightly tilts up, freezing at the peak moment of shared completion, forming a coherent and vibrant conclusion.

prompts: Shot 1 opens directly with a medium-long shot, eye-level tracking composition. Tree trunks and leaves pass through the foreground, while the background features a sun-dappled mountain path. Shallow depth of field focuses on the girl child carrying a small backpack. She walks quickly and urgently, shoulders tense. The grandmother reaches out from the side rear of the frame to offer a jacket, but the girl sharply shakes it off and continues forward. The jacket fabric swings briefly in an arc, and the backpack sways slightly due to momentum.

Shot 2 transitions via hard cut to a bend in the mountain road, using a medium shot with a slight high-angle lateral tracking view. The guardrail and slope form a curved composition, with focus shifting between grandmother and granddaughter. Occasionally, wind-blown grass blades sweep across the foreground. The girl stubbornly turns aside, refusing eye contact, lifting her chin higher. Their distance alternates between widening and narrowing as they chase and evade. Lighting remains consistent warm natural light. The camera performs minor pans and slight wobbles, emphasizing the undulating terrain and physical exertion.

Shot 3 transitions emotionally via fade-in to the seaside mountain-top viewing platform, using a dolly-in from long shot to close-up: first a wide, eye-level shot establishes the platform, bench, railing, and golden sea in the distance, then slowly zooms into a close-up. The girl sits alone at one end of the bench, her back small and isolated, the surrounding space amplified by sea breeze and emptiness. She lowers her head, quietly wiping tears with her sleeve, shoulders rising and falling gently. Her backpack rests beside her, its zipper pull lightly tapping the surface in the wind, producing a tiny metallic The composition leaves the other side of the bench empty, suggesting an emotional gap. Lighting begins to incorporate more pronounced sunset edge light. The dolly-in slows, allowing emotion to settle.

Shot 4 follows via a soft hard cut, using a close-up to extreme close-up with a slight low angle. Focus first lands on the old scarf in the grandmother’s hands, then shifts to the girl’s moistened eyes. The scarf’s edge glows softly in backlight, revealing delicate fiber texture. As it settles on her shoulders, the girl’s body tenses slightly at first, then stops resisting. Her fingers instinctively grasp a corner of the scarf, signaling emotional thaw. The camera slowly pushes in and slightly tilts upward. Sunset backlight outlines both figures with a soft golden glow. The overall emotion shifts from hurt to comfort.

Shot 5 transitions via fade-in/fade-out to the closing shot, using a medium-long shot with a rear-facing eye-level tracking view. The forest descent path reappears, echoing the opening, but with a calmer, broader composition. Foreground foliage is illuminated by evening light, while layered forests in the background gradually blur. The grandmother and girl walk down side by side, their steps now more synchronized. The girl first glances at her grandmother’s hand, then reaches out and takes it. The grandmother gently returns the grip. Their hands become the new visual focal point in the center of the frame. The scarf sways gently with each step, and the backpack no longer jolts violently. The camera performs a steady backward tracking shot with slight panning, guiding the pair from tension into unified forward motion. The final image holds on their backs as they continue descending hand in hand, completing a full and coherent emotional reconciliation.

prompts: Shot 1 opens with a fade-in, using a wide high-angle composition to establish the subway entrance. Signage, escalators, and cold white lights form clear leading lines. Blurred pedestrians pass in the foreground, while focus centers on a girl standing before the map, holding it upside down. Her expression is serious yet confused, illuminated by cold fluorescent light that emphasizes her embarrassment. She tilts her head slightly, tracing an incorrect direction with her finger, muttering "え、こっち？" softly. The camera slowly pushes in to medium-close, emphasizing her unawareness of the mistake.

Shot 2 cuts hard from the previous shot, using a medium eye-level tracking shot. The turnstile is centered as an obstacle, with blurred card-swiping crowds in the foreground and cold-colored lighting strips extending into the background. The girl suddenly charges forward, but the end of her scarf gets caught in the turnstile edge, pulling her back abruptly. She stumbles backward, her scarf and coat hem flung upward by inertia. She turns sharply and shouts “ち、違います！” urgently to the staff. The staff is off-screen, glancing toward her.

Shot 3 cuts hard via action-matched direction, opening with a wide-medium eye-level view from the side of the platform. Platform edges, warning lines, and lit posters create depth. The arriving train generates strong wind pressure, with cold blue reflections flowing across the floor. The girl has just freed her scarf and hasn’t stabilized when she’s blown sideways by the gust, crashing into a promotional poster frame. Her face and shoulders press against the transparent panel, hair and scarf whipping wildly. The camera quickly pans to follow her trajectory, creating exaggerated yet fluid physical comedy.

Shot 4 cuts hard into the exit area, starting with a wide high-angle shot showing her path after leaving the platform. On the left is the real subway exit; on the right, a sign pointing to the museum corridor. Cold lighting continues. The girl adjusts her scarf, still dazed from the wind. She walks quickly, mistaking the museum sign for a subway exit and rushing into the corridor. Foreground pedestrians naturally part, forming a false route. The background shifts from metallic subway walls to cultural facility corridors, maintaining logical continuity. The camera slowly tilts down from above and follows her into the corridor, completing the scene transition.

A close-up eye-level composition places the girl on the right, with a slow-moving cleaning robot on the left. Floor reflections and tall ceilings create a clean, calm space. Soft overhead lighting maintains the cool tone. The hall’s echo subtly amplifies her polite request. The camera gently pushes in to near close-up, capturing her sincere yet absurd expression.

The camera then rapidly tilts down to medium shot. She looks up, sees the shadow looming, pupils shrink, shoulders jerk—instinctively opening her umbrella. The ribs flash briefly in the cold light, exaggerating her mistaken perception of the exhibit as a threat.

Shot 7 cuts via action continuity from the umbrella’s opening direction. It starts with a close-up shifting to medium, the camera eye-level and close to the umbrella tip. The sharp tip is in the foreground, with a brochure stand blurred in the background. The girl steps back in panic, and the tip sweeps across, knocking over the stand. The fall angle and paper flight paths form a fan-shaped spread across the frame. Pages fly like snowflakes, reflecting tiny bright spots under cold light. She instinctively reaches out, making her movements even messier. The camera quickly pans sideways and slightly pulls back, revealing the full scope of chaos.

Shot 8 cuts hard from the previous shot. A low-angle close-up shoots downward at the ground. Among scattered brochures, a small ticket-like paper slides across the smooth floor, becoming the visual focus. The girl rushes after it, her shoe catching on loose papers and slipping. She lurches forward, stopping only at a “请勿触摸” warning sign. One hand hangs mid-air, one foot swings back, umbrella handle and scarf swinging unbalanced. The entire motion—from chase to abrupt halt—is clearly visible. Background display cases and warning lines remain identifiable. The camera rapidly tracks forward along a ground rail, intensifying the sense of uncontrolled slide.

Shot 9 cuts hard to a reaction shot. A medium eye-level shot uses slight reverse-angle framing. In the foreground left, the girl is frozen in a comical pose before the “请勿触摸” sign. In the background right, a staff member and several scattered visitors are present. They misinterpret her sequence of actions as an impromptu performance. The girl’s eyes go blank, then gradually realize the misunderstanding. Her lips twitch. The camera first slightly pushes toward the staff, then pans back to her reaction, making the misunderstanding feel natural and complete.

Shot 10 cuts hard to conclude. A close-up eye-level slightly low-angle shot centers the girl. Behind her, the towering dinosaur skeleton and a few still-falling brochures form a humorous curtain-call backdrop. prompts: The first shot begins with a fade-in, presenting a wide overhead view with slight pan of the zero-gravity spacecraft observation cabin. A silver-blue square paper floats in the foreground, while a completed starbird crane hovers nearby as a reference model. In the background, a curved viewport reveals slowly drifting starfields.

The second shot connects to the previous shot with a hard cut, transitioning to an overhead close-up. The camera remains stable above the worktable, centered on the silver-blue square paper. Hands enter from both sides of the frame. The foreground shows only hands and paper, while the background blurs into cool blue cabin walls and floating small objects. Shallow depth of field makes the fold lines extremely clear. The astronaut first folds the square diagonally into a triangle, then folds it again to create a central crease. As fingertips press along the edge, subtle changes in paper reflection are visible. Auxiliary lighting evenly illuminates the creases. The camera slightly lowers and performs a very gentle follow pan, ensuring precise and easy-to-follow step demonstration.

The third shot transitions from the previous shot with a brief hard cut into a hand extreme close-up. The camera is slightly overhead and eye-level, focusing on the central crease of the paper. The foreground shows the unfolded square paper, while the background is completely blurred into cool-colored bokeh. The paper gradually transforms from flat to a neat diamond shape. Fingers quickly yet gently smooth the creases. The silver-blue paper sparkles subtly under the cool light like metal. The The camera slightly pushes in, further emphasizing alignment of corners and formation of creases.

The fourth shot transitions from the previous shot via a smooth action match to a medium-close eye-level angle. The upper body of the character re-enters the frame. The background reveals the curved structure of the observation cabin and floating instrument lights. Foreground, midground, and background are clearly layered: the foreground shows the diamond-shaped paper held in her palm, the midground shows her focused face and hands working together, and the background features the cool blue viewport light band. The astronaut performs reverse inward folds to form the head and tail of the paper crane, then gently spreads the wings outward. The movements are fluid and clear, transforming the compact angular shape into a three-dimensional bird-like structure. Lighting remains primarily cold natural light, with only soft highlights outlining the paper edges. The camera uses a slow, small-scale orbital pan to emphasize the transformation from flat to three-dimensional.

The fifth shot transitions from the previous shot with a fade-in/fade-out effect to a close-up in front of the viewport. The camera is slightly low-angle, focusing on the completed starbird crane held in her palm. The foreground shows the clear outline of her hand and the crane, the midground shows her satisfied and gentle expression, and the background features the deep blue starfield and distant nebulae. The composition places the crane in front of the bright area of the viewport, creating a distinct silhouette and metallic reflection. She gently releases her fingers, allowing the crane to float slowly toward the window in zero gravity. The wings flutter slightly in minor air currents. The final product is fully displayed. The camera slowly pulls out, concluding the tutorial naturally with the completed artwork and poetic space imagery.

prompts: Shot 1 begins with a fade-in from black into the concourse establishing shot, using a wide eye-level composition. Shot 2 follows with a hard cut from the previous shot, transitioning to a medium-close side-eye-level view. The camera moves slowly along the corridor toward his playing direction. Occasionally blurred pillars and passing light boxes sweep across the foreground. Focus remains firmly on his right hand and the guitar soundhole. Station light strips in the background blur into cool-colored bokeh. Cold white fluorescence remains dominant lighting; wood grain on the guitar surface appears dry and realistic under low-contrast reflection. His right hand transitions naturally from open-string strumming to clear up-down strumming. Mechanical hums and strum textures interlock seamlessly.

Shot 3 enters via a hard cut from the prior shot into a close-up of hand technique, using a tight overhead-side angle. The fretboard diagonally slices across the frame. Background is darkened into a cool blue blurred platform space. Main light still comes from overhead fixtures, creating narrow highlights along finger edges. Performance advances into continuous up-down strumming in the main section, followed by muted hammer-ons in the secondary section. The camera uses extremely subtle macro push and focus shift to follow fingers sliding from 3rd to 7th fret and back, reinforcing technical continuity.

Subject is positioned slightly right of center. In the background, train headlights approach from distance, converging toward him and the guitar. Depth lines draw attention inward. Shot 5 connects via a soft fade transition at the moment the train stops, shifting to a close-up eye-level ending. His right hand gradually narrows the final chord sequence from full strumming. Left hand releases pressure. Final harmonics resonate and echo in the empty platform. Surrounding mechanical hums return to the foreground. The camera performs an extremely slow directional push until it stops between his slightly lowered face and guitar neck, concluding the solo in quiet, reserved reverberation.

prompts: Shot 1 opens with a fade-in from black, a wide overhead shot of the medieval castle tower at night. Low-saturation watercolor edges make the stone texture appear softly diffused like paper in a picture book. Cold night surrounds the warm glow. The camera slowly pushes forward along the tower wall, drawing viewers toward the glowing window.

Shot 2 hard cuts from previous shot to interior of the castle, a full shot eye-level capturing a boy walking through a narrow corridor toward the alchemy table. Arched stone columns frame both sides, forming leading lines. Old bricks on the floor reflect candlelight. Occasionally, a wall sconce passes through foreground, creating soft obstruction. Focus remains steady on the small bottle he holds and his steps. Warm candlelight remains dominant, while faint cold blue reflections are visible from the far end of the lab. The camera performs smooth lateral tracking, conveying spatial continuity from corridor to alchemy room.

Shot 3 transitions from previous shot with brief fade to close-up overhead view focusing on the alchemy table surface. On the wooden table are several small bottles, salt powders, metal spoons, and a small furnace. Foreground shows blurred edge of a half-open wooden box. Focus shifts slowly from labeled bottle tops to the boy’s fingers as he arranges powder in neat piles. Powder particles retain dry, fine texture even under watercolor rendering. The furnace is not yet lit. Candlelight from side-rear highlights subtle surface undulations. The camera uses extremely slow overhead drift and slight focus shift to present the precise sequence of preparation.

Shot 4 hard cuts from previous shot to close-up eye-level shot. The furnace opening occupies center-lower frame. The boy brings an ignition tool near the wick. Foreground shows a small pile of unused powder blurred into pale patches. The first orange flame leaps up instantly upon contact, sparks briefly scatter then quickly retract. Warm light immediately overwhelms the dim surroundings, illuminating his fingertips and furnace rim. The camera makes a brief push-in, locking onto the instant the flame forms.

Shot 5 transitions from previous shot via action match to macro close-up overhead view. The boy gently sprinkles the first type of powder into the orange flame. Shallow depth of field makes the powder’s trajectory into the flame the absolute focal point. Originally orange flame rapidly turns green and curls upward. Color change starts from base and spreads to tip. Warm candlelight still casts soft shadows in background.

Shot 6 hard cuts from previous shot to close-up eye-level shot. Another small spoon delivers copper salt to the edge of the small furnace. Foreground shows blurred blue-gray outline of a glass bottle. Focus is on the slender flame tongue. New flame shows colder blue at root and extends higher and thinner, gently swaying in air currents. Flame edges are transparent, center brighter, forming a clear and continuous experimental progression from previous green flame. Environment remains dual illumination of candlelight and colored flames. Gentle glass and metal clinks interject. Camera performs very controlled lateral micro-move, making blue flame appear to glide quietly within frame.

Shot 7 transitions from previous shot with soft fade to medium overhead view. Multiple small bottles are neatly arranged on wooden table. Flame tongues in different furnaces vary in height. Orange, green, and blue flames create layered rhythmic progression on same surface. Foreground shows unopened bottle stopper. Background features softly blurred stone wall and pages. Focus centers on silhouette of staggered flame tips. Overhead composition makes experimental order immediately clear. Candlelight warms wood grain. Colored flames cast alternating warm and cool shadows on table. Camera performs slow overhead drift, scanning left to right across entire row of flames, ensuring each form is fully visible.

Shot 8 hard cuts from previous shot to close-up eye-level slightly overhead angle. Boy lifts glass cover from top of frame and slowly lowers it over one flame. Foreground shows reflection on transparent glass edge. Background is blurred bookshelf and stone wall. Focus locks on flame shape changing within cover. Originally scattered flame gradually becomes narrower, straighter, and more stable under cover. Blue-green light spots shimmer on glass surface. Emotion here slightly pauses. Camera performs slight downward tilt and push-in, emphasizing observation action and subtle changes in constrained flame.

Frame focuses on boy’s face. He slightly raises head, watching flame color inside glass cover. Blue, green, and red reflections successively illuminate his cheeks, eyelashes, and eyes. Occasional out-of-focus flame tongue passes through foreground, naturally linking character and experimental result. Background alchemy room recedes into soft color blocks. Candlelight maintains warm base tone on skin. Colored flames leave dreamy, controlled cool highlights on face.

Shot 10 transitions from previous shot with fade-in/fade-out to wide full shot eye-level with slight pull-back. Entire alchemy room appears like a quiet page from a picture book. Composition centers alchemy table slightly forward, with night outside tower window in distant background. A stationary glass cover in foreground echoes earlier scene. Focus expands gradually from person and flames to entire room, restoring calmness. Warm candlelight and cool flame light continue to unify the scene. Camera slowly pulls back and slightly elevates, freezing the entire lab in low-saturation watercolor texture as a tranquil and mysterious conclusion.

prompts: Shot 1 opens directly into the frame with a wide eye-level composition showing the classroom lab bench, blackboard in the background, cold daylight from the window, and neatly arranged beakers. A blurred test tube rack in the foreground adds depth. The overall lighting is cool and even.

Shot 2 cuts hard from the previous shot to a close-up side view, framing her upper body and hands. Side light slants in from the window, creating cold white highlights on the beaker's edge. The background is softly blurred, preserving the classroom outline. Focus is locked on the pipette in her hand and the other cup containing pale blue reagent. She steadily lifts her hand and drops the transparent liquid one drop at a time into the cup. The camera makes a very controlled micro-following pan, allowing viewers to clearly see the fine ripples before and after the transparent liquid enters the pale blue solution.

Shot 3 cuts hard via action match to an overhead close-up. The lab bench surface is neatly laid out, with the edges of the vessels forming intersecting circular and diagonal graphic patterns. Shallow depth of field focuses all attention on the internal changes of the liquid. Under cool light, the two liquids rapidly fuse in the container, changing color quickly from light blue to deeper purple. Fine thread-like swirls appear first at the center, followed by gradual thickening, pulling out sticky textures, and forming a translucent gel-like consistency. Surface reflections shift from scattered moving highlights to more continuous moist shine. The camera remains stable in overhead view, making only a minimal push-in to enhance the realism of the material transition.

Shot 4 transitions smoothly via a lateral dolly move from the lab bench to the window-side record table. In a medium-close eye-level composition, the window frame and table edge form clear horizontal and vertical lines. The background is a softly defocused corner of the classroom. Cold natural light becomes more prominent on her goggles and the beaker surface. She shows a surprised expression, eyes slightly widened, humming lightly while gently swaying the beaker to observe the slow flow of the semi-solid substance inside. The gel-like liquid leaves a viscous trail on the cup wall before slowly retracting, clearly indicating a distinct semi-solid state change. The subtle The camera continues its dolly movement and slightly stabilizes, making the observation motion feel coherent and natural.

Shot 5 transitions gently via a soft fade-in/fade-out into a near close-up. The camera focuses on her raised hands holding the result and half her smiling face under natural cool light by the window. The composition centers the beaker visually, with sharp foreground and completely softened background. Cold daylight passes through the container, giving the internal substance a sparkling translucent quality. The previously purple gel-like material appears in stillness with a delicate jelly-like coagulated texture, its surface highlight stable and clear, as if frozen in light. She raises the result high and slightly rotates it to confirm the color. Joy overcomes tension, aligning with the freeze-frame presentation of the result. The camera makes one final slow push-in, stopping at the moment the crystalline texture is most vivid, completing the display of the experimental outcome.

The character’s upper body is on the left, while the phone and two core function buttons appear in the right foreground. The interface framework expands from single to multi-layered. Background daylight is dimmed half-stop to emphasize screen glow.

Shot 7 connects via an interface particle burst transition, switching to a full wide overhead shot. The character stands at the edge of a high platform, beneath a data waterfall and widespread gold rain falling between heaven and earth. Numbers, icons, and task emblems cascade down like pixel runes. Occasionally, gold coins fly past the lens, adding depth. Distant palaces and clouds maintain consistent warm gold tones. When the phone is raised, it acts as a luminous source, drawing data streams outward. The background forms a multi-layered stage-like space composed of heavenly gates, rainbow bridges, and floating interfaces. Semi-transparent buttons and title boxes glide across the foreground. The midground features the glowing phone, while the background shows layered functional panels. Warm light from the front and side-back simultaneously outlines facial and shoulder contours. Buttons, labels, and badges appear densely but remain clearly organized.

Shot 9 concludes with a fade-out followed by a quick fade-in transition, cutting to a full frontal eye-level shot. The character freezes in front of the majestic heavenly gate, holding the phone slightly angled toward the camera. The gate serves as a symmetrical backdrop, with cloud seas flowing slowly below. All floating interfaces converge toward the center and transform into the final brand closure. The LOGO appears at the top-center, crafted in jade-inlaid gold pixel material with soft radiant glow emanating from within. Text "现在下载" is centered below, in bold lettering with sparkling outlines. Its entrance animation involves a shrink-and-bounce effect accompanied by tiny star dust. Residual gold coins and data particles linger around as decorative finishers. The character holds a confident, bright pose. The final The camera slowly pulls back and stops at the end, leaving the LOGO, slogan, and product image fully centered in the frame.

prompts: Shot 1 opens with a hard cut to a wide eye-level composition. Foreground features slightly swaying shrubs and tree trunks; midground shows an elderly woman standing alone at the edge of a forest at the mountain base; background faintly reveals the outline of the volcano. The depth of the forest creates leading lines, while light mist and dust enhance spatial layers. Natural light spreads evenly, and scattered leaves on the ground vibrate subtly.

Shot 2 connects via a hard cut to a wide overhead-to-eye-level tracking shot. The distant crater gradually comes into focus, emitting swirling black smoke and intermittent red glows. Natural light remains dominant, but sky brightness is dimmed by smoke, and red reflections begin to appear along rock edges. The camera steadily tracks her path and slightly tilts upward at the end of the sentence, fully framing the crater.

Shot 3 transitions via a hard cut to a close-up to near-extreme close-up eye-level shot. Her face dominates the frame. Slight air distortion caused by heat waves appears in the foreground, while the background blurs into churning molten lava and glowing fissures. Shallow depth of field keeps focus tightly on her wrinkled face, subtle eye twitching, and skin texture illuminated by red light. Lighting continues the dual tone of natural light and volcanic red glow, with red light sweeping across one side of her face, enhancing the sense of imminent danger. She instinctively steps back half a step, her gaze crossing over the lens toward the crack below, urgently warning “别靠近裂口”.

Shot 4 connects via a hard cut to a medium eye-level tracking pan shot. The character rapidly retreats from left to right across a black volcanic wasteland. Rough, charred rocks pass in the foreground, while a bright river of lava flows down scorched earth in the midground. Smoke continues to rise from the lower slopes in the background. Overall lighting remains unchanged—natural daylight suppresses the vast gray-black terrain, while red-orange reflections from the lava’s heat flicker across the ground and the edges of her clothing. She turns her head to observe while quickly retreating, her hem fluttering in the hot wind, her steps clearly faster. The camera continuously pans with a slight handheld feel, accurately recording changes in speed and terrain elevation.

Shot 5 connects via a fade-in transition to a long-medium eye-level rear view composition. The character stands before a black rocky shoreline, facing away from the camera, forming a stable vertical center. The foreground features wet rocks and rolling seawater, while in the background, lava pours into the sea, rising in large plumes of white steam and turbulent vapor. The horizon and steam clouds create an open layered depth. The color tone remains predominantly neutral cool gray, with only the point where lava meets water bursting into brighter orange-red. High-temperature steam glows softly at the backlit edges. The camera first slowly pushes in on her back and gesture, then slightly tilts upward to include the steam and sky, completing a continuous observational record from surface activity to lava entering the sea.

prompts: Shot 1 opens directly with a wide eye-level shot. Chicken cubes, green onions, ginger, garlic, cucumber, peanuts, and seasoning bowls are neatly laid out. The background features a bright, clean kitchen cabinet and stove. Warm natural light evenly illuminates the surface.

Shot 2 connects with the previous shot via a hard cut, switching to a medium close-up overhead view. The cutting board dominates the frame, with ingredients arranged in sequence across foreground and background. Focus remains locked on the intersection of hands and knife blade. The kitchen background is de-emphasized to maintain instructional clarity. Warm lighting remains consistent. The chicken is cleanly diced into uniform cubes, followed by separate cuts of green onions, ginger, garlic, and cucumber. She simultaneously explains “鸡肉切丁，葱姜蒜和黄瓜分别备好”. The camera remains mostly static, with only minimal follow pan to ensure full visibility of actions.

Shot 3 connects with the previous shot via a hard cut, using a close-up overhead view. A glass bowl is centered in the frame, with spoons and seasonings in the foreground and a softly blurred background preserving countertop texture. Lighting remains warm and soft, creating clean reflections on the bowl’s surface. The young woman adds salt, cooking wine, and starch to the chicken, then rapidly mixes by hand. The chicken transitions from loose to moist and evenly coated. Precise interaction between fingers and ingredients is clearly visible. The camera performs a slight push-in to emphasize textural changes.

Shot 4 connects with the previous shot via a hard cut, transitioning to a medium close-up overhead view. A small seasoning bowl is centered in composition. Sugar, vinegar, soy sauce, and a small amount of starch are added sequentially, forming clear procedural layers. Background remains the same countertop environment, with unchanged lighting. Liquids are stirred with chopsticks, quickly blending from layered to uniformly translucent. The camera performs a slight overhead circular movement to help viewers observe the mixture state.

Shot 5 connects with the previous shot via a hard cut, shifting to a medium close-up slightly angled downward. The stove and pot opening occupy the right side of the frame, with a strainer and empty plate on the left for depth. Side lighting highlights the pot edge and peanut surface. The young woman pours peanuts into hot oil on low heat, gently frying them. Peanuts move slightly in oil, turning more golden. They are quickly scooped out with a strainer and removed. She explains “花生小火炸香，先盛出来保持脆感”. The camera performs a short lateral pan along the pot edge, then gently pushes in to emphasize heat control.

Shot 6 connects with the previous shot via a hard cut, using a medium eye-level slightly side-angle view. The pot surface becomes the absolute focal point. The edge of the spatula appears in the foreground, while the background stove remains simple. Under warm light, the oil surface reflects soft, bright highlights. After heating the pan and adding oil, dried chilies and Sichuan peppercorns are added. The spices jump rapidly in oil, releasing aroma and instantly activating their color. She clearly announces in Chinese “锅里留底油，下干辣椒和花椒，小火爆香”. The camera performs a slight tilt-follow from the pot edge, enhancing the layered impact of spices hitting the oil.

Shot 7 connects with the previous shot via a hard cut, switching to a medium close-up slightly upward angle with a noticeable push-in. After chicken is added to the pot, it occupies the center of the frame. Steam and spatula form dynamic foreground obstructions. Background kitchen lights blur into soft warm spots. The chicken rapidly changes from translucent to opaque and shiny, edges slightly curling. Sleeve and steam follow movements realistically. The camera continuously pushes forward, reinforcing the sense of speed and transformation during stir-frying.

Shot 8 connects with the previous shot via a hard cut, employing a composite motion from overhead to eye-level. Composition guides diced cucumber, peanuts, and sauce entering the pot from the top of the frame. Ingredients inside the pot form distinct color layers. Warm main lighting remains consistent, creating wet reflections on the sauce surface. The young woman quickly adds diced cucumber, returned peanuts, and prepared sauce. The spatula continuously flips ingredients, efficiently mixing them over high heat. Cucumber retains crispness, peanuts stay firm, and sauce begins to adhere. The camera first slightly lowers, then follows the stir-fry direction with a lateral pan, emphasizing critical heat control in the tutorial.

Shot 9 connects with the previous shot via match-cut editing, transitioning to a close-up eye-level view. A partial section of the pot fills the frame. Shallow depth of field keeps focus firmly on chicken and sauce surface. Background is fully blurred into warm color blocks. Sauce transitions from flowing to thickened, bubbles become finer, and glossy sheen evenly coats chicken, cucumber, and peanuts. Material changes are clearly discernible. She slows her pace, stating “看到汤汁收亮、均匀挂住食材就可以了”. The camera performs a macro-style slow push-in, clearly conveying the crucial pre-completion state.

Shot 10 gently dissolves from the previous shot, using a medium-long shot at eye level that slowly pulls back. The finished dish is transferred from the wok to a white plate on a wooden table. In the foreground, the freshly plated Kung Pao chicken is displayed, while the background reveals the still-bright and warm kitchen environment. Finely chopped green onions are evenly sprinkled over the top as the final touch. A young woman stands in front of the wooden table, looking directly at the camera, and concludes with a natural and friendly tone “这样做出来鸡丁嫩、花生脆、口感酸甜微辣，关键就是花生先盛出，最后大火快速收汁”. The soft The camera slowly pulls back, fully revealing the finished dish, the person, and the surrounding environment, bringing the tutorial to a clear and satisfying conclusion.

prompts: Shot 1 opens with a fade-in, using a steady eye-level wide shot that slowly pushes in. A wooden table by the window is positioned slightly below center, creating a balanced composition. In the foreground, a neat tabletop holds several sheets of colored paper. The background features a window frame illuminated by warm sunlight and softly blurred indoor corners. The focus rests on the upper body of a young woman and the props on the table. She wears a natural smile, holding up a completed paper crane with her left hand and displaying a square sheet of colored paper with her right. The camera slowly moves forward, allowing viewers to clearly see the proportion between the material and the finished product. The paper gently trembles at her fingertips, and soft highlights form along the crease edges under the light.

The second shot cuts abruptly from the previous one, transitioning to an overhead close-up. The wooden grain of the tabletop spreads horizontally as a clear background, with a tight composition where the colored paper dominates the frame. In shallow depth of field, the hands and edges of the paper are most sharply defined. She carefully folds the square sheet of colored paper along its diagonal, slowly aligning the two corners and then pressing down from the center toward both ends with her fingertips to create a crisp crease, while softly explaining “先沿对角线对折，对齐四角，再把中间的折痕压实”. Warm natural light slants in from the upper left of the frame, casting shadows along the fold that help viewers perceive the structural change.

The third shot enters with a sharp cut from the previous one, using an overhead close-up with a slightly wider framing to fully capture the unfolding motion of both hands. The composition uses the central axis of the paper as a visual guide. The paper transitions from a triangular shape into a more three-dimensional diamond structure, while the Chinese The camera follows her hand movements with a subtle downward tracking motion, ensuring that each alignment, pinch, and smoothing action remains in focus.

Shot 4 connects to the previous shot with a soft, continuous motion cut, transitioning to a level close-up from a front-side angle that captures the crucial steps in forming the paper crane into a three-dimensional shape. In the foreground, her fingers steadily support the body of the paper crane, with focus placed on the tip and the crease junctions. The background window light is softly blurred into warm highlights. As she folds, she quietly explains in Chinese “现在把一端翻出颈部，另一端翻出尾部，折的时候慢一点，角度尽量对称”, gently pinching the lower part of the paper and pulling apart while flipping both ends in opposite directions, gradually creating a difference in length between the neck and tail sections. The camera performs a slight lateral pan and a subtle push-in, emphasizing the opening, folding, and shaping of the paper layers. Sharp creases become more pronounced under pressure, with clear and detailed movements shown without any skipped steps.

Shot 5 concludes with a soft fade-in/fade-out transition from the previous shot, using a close-up pull-back to capture the young woman returning naturally to her wooden desk by the window. The composition begins with her finished paper crane in hand, initially focusing on the crane's head and wings, then gradually pulling back to include her posture as she holds it up along with the tabletop. She gently spreads the wings fully, allowing the silhouette of the paper crane to unfold completely, then lifts it to chest height with both hands, smiling as she summarizes in Chinese “最后把翅膀轻轻展开，一只纸鹤就完成了，跟着步骤慢慢做就可以”. As the camera pulls back, viewers get a full view of the final result and the working environment.

prompts: Shot 1 opens with a fade-in from black, using a wide overhead perspective showing the dome, suspended skeletal exhibits, and the museum hall repurposed as a courtroom. Benches, evidence table, and judge's bench align along the central tile axis, forming strong leading lines. Foreground features security gates and metal barriers; midground shows seating rows; background includes the high dome and stained glass. Soft daylight pours down, reflecting faint warm gold on the stone floor. A golden-scaled dragon passes through the security gate, its scales rendered in flowing watercolor layers. It folds its wings and slows its pace toward the defense seat, tail lightly brushing the ground and causing paper edges to tremble. audience murmurs remain subdued, as if absorbed by the dome. The camera slowly pushes forward and slightly tilts down, transitioning from grand display to immediate courtroom presence.

Shot 2 follows previous shot with a hard cut, switching to medium-close eye-level view focused on the evidence table. Blurred microphone and document edges in foreground frame the scene. Midground shows a fire-feathered phoenix standing before the prosecution bench; background holds blurred jury silhouettes. Side light from the dome glides over feather tips, creating glowing watercolor halos around red-gold plumage. The phoenix lifts a wing and steadily presents a cracked gemstone, its interior filled with fine luminous patterns resembling sealed embers. The other wing gently sweeps across documents, causing the evidence label to sway slightly. The action pauses clearly between reveal and stillness. The camera pushes along the evidence table axis, stopping at a distance where both the gem’s crack and the phoenix’s sharp gaze are sharply defined.

Shot 3 follows previous shot with a hard cut to adjacent exhibit hall, using medium side-eye-level view. Left side shows a broken glass display case; right side features a hanging monitor. The dragon stands slightly forward-center. The shattered edge of the case forms a sharp silhouette in the foreground; the monitor’s timestamp glows steadily in the background. Cold blue-gray walls and warm exhibit lights maintain the same watercolor aesthetic. The dragon raises its front claw toward the monitor, then smoothly turns toward the gap in the case, forming a clear counter-evidence chain. Dust particles become visible in the side light as the claw moves. The image emphasizes the mismatch between theft site and surveillance time. The camera first pans slightly to follow the dragon’s gesture, then performs a minor push-in, aligning the monitor timestamp and case damage into a shared visual focus.

Shot 4 enters climax via rapid hard cut, using extreme close-up low-angle view. Distance is compressed dramatically. Foreground shows slightly out-of-focus document corners and edge of evidence table. Midground features the golden-scaled dragon and fire-feathered phoenix advancing toward confrontation under dome-side lighting. Scales and feathers reflect cold and warm high-saturation hues respectively. Background shows only a sliver of illuminated dome arc. Shallow depth of field focuses on eyes, throat movements, wingtips, and claws trembling subtly. The phoenix steps forward half a pace, wings slightly open; The two freeze abruptly after intense approach, creating a suspended moment before climax. Instantly, a gavel strike from off-screen silences the room—a sharp, crisp hit cuts all commotion. The camera makes a very short push-in and slight upward tilt, delivering both courtroom authority and conflict pressure simultaneously.

Shot 5 transitions to resolution via hard cut triggered by gavel Judge’s bench dominates center-high position, forming absolute visual focus. Foreground shows softly undulating audience silhouettes; midground features the phoenix retracting wings and stepping back, while the dragon remains at its seat. Background shows the towering stone griffin judge raising a claw and stamping the seal under dome daylight. The seal impact causes document edges to vibrate uniformly. Warm gold side light sweeps across the judge’s stone wings, grounding the verdict’s solemnity within the watercolor texture. Dragon’s shoulder muscles relax from tension; phoenix slowly folds wings, head lowered. Gavel echo, dull seal thud, and audience murmur form the closing The camera slowly pulls back while slightly rising, reuniting the post-acquittal reaction with the museum courtroom beneath the vast dome, completing the narrative loop.
